title: Name a step
prompt: Using a CTE named dept_totals, total salaries per department_id as total, then show rows with a total above 100000. Replace the ___.
starterSql:
WITH dept_totals AS (
  SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total
  FROM employees
  GROUP BY department_id
)
SELECT department_id, total
FROM ___
WHERE total > 100000;
hints: The main query reads the CTE like a table.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: WITH dept_totals AS (SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees GROUP BY department_id) SELECT department_id, total FROM dept_totals WHERE total > 100000;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH dept_totals AS (SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees GROUP BY department_id) SELECT department_id, total FROM dept_totals;
WITH dept_totals AS (SELECT department_id, MAX(salary) AS total FROM employees GROUP BY department_id) SELECT department_id, total FROM dept_totals WHERE total > 100000;

title: Join a CTE
prompt: With a CTE of units per order, show each customer_id and total units as units.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: WITH t AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(t.units) AS units FROM orders o JOIN t ON t.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(t.units) AS units FROM orders o JOIN t ON t.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS units FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

title: Two steps
prompt: Use two CTEs: dept_avg for each department's average salary, and overall for the average of all salaries. Show the department_id of departments averaging above the overall average.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) AS average FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY department_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(salary) AS average FROM employees) SELECT d.department_id FROM dept_avg d, overall o WHERE d.average > o.average;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) AS average FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY department_id) SELECT department_id FROM dept_avg;
wrongSolutions.why: Doesn't compare with the overall average

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH dept_avg AS (SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) AS average FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY department_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(salary) AS average FROM employees) SELECT d.department_id FROM dept_avg d, overall o WHERE d.average < o.average;

title: Passing students
prompt: With a CTE of each student's average grade, show the name of students averaging at least 70.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); UPDATE enrolments SET grade = 80 WHERE id = 11; UPDATE enrolments SET grade = 60 WHERE id = 12; INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 8, 5, 69, '2024-spring');

solutions: WITH a AS (SELECT student_id, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id) SELECT s.name FROM students s JOIN a ON a.student_id = s.id WHERE a.average >= 70;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT student_id, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id) SELECT s.name FROM students s JOIN a ON a.student_id = s.id WHERE a.average > 70;
SELECT s.name FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id WHERE e.grade >= 70;

title: Empty step
prompt: With a CTE of cancelled orders, show how many of them each customer_id has as cancelled, only for customers appearing in it. Customers with none don't appear.
hints: A CTE can be small, or empty.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: WITH c AS (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled') SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS cancelled FROM c GROUP BY customer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS cancelled FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;
WITH c AS (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'shipped') SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS cancelled FROM c GROUP BY customer_id;

title: Fix the WITH
prompt: This should use a CTE named top to find the highest salary, then show who earns it, but it fails. Fix it.
starterSql:
WITH top SELECT MAX(salary) AS salary FROM employees
SELECT e.name
FROM employees e
JOIN top ON top.salary = e.salary;
hints: Every WITH needs AS and brackets.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: WITH top AS (SELECT MAX(salary) AS salary FROM employees) SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN top ON top.salary = e.salary;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH top AS (SELECT MIN(salary) AS salary FROM employees) SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN top ON top.salary = e.salary;

title: Step by step revenue
prompt: Use a CTE to calculate line revenue (price times quantity) per order_id as revenue, then show the average order revenue as avg_revenue, rounded to 2 decimals.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: WITH r AS (SELECT i.order_id, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY i.order_id) SELECT ROUND(AVG(revenue), 2) AS avg_revenue FROM r;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(p.price * i.quantity), 2) AS avg_revenue FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;
WITH r AS (SELECT i.order_id, SUM(p.price) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY i.order_id) SELECT ROUND(AVG(revenue), 2) AS avg_revenue FROM r;

title: Course leaderboard
prompt: Using CTEs, find each course_id's average grade and the highest such average. Show the title of each course matching the highest average.
hints: One CTE for averages, then compare with MAX.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: WITH a AS (SELECT course_id, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id) SELECT c.title FROM a JOIN courses c ON c.id = a.course_id WHERE a.average = (SELECT MAX(average) FROM a);

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT course_id, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id) SELECT c.title FROM a JOIN courses c ON c.id = a.course_id;
WITH a AS (SELECT course_id, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id) SELECT c.title FROM a JOIN courses c ON c.id = a.course_id WHERE a.average = (SELECT MIN(average) FROM a);
